Scenario 5 Tech Fund Calculation Multiple items

Kevin has worked at X-Horst garages for 6 months with 64 colleagues. Following a workplace assessment, he has been awarded multiple items. The support includes:

an adapted wheelchair costing £10,000

a desktop PC with assistive technology costing £8000

a hearing aid costing £3000

He works 4 days a week and will be benefiting from the wheelchair and hearing aid both at work and on his non-working days; the PC will remain in his workplace. He does not have an NHS voucher/PWB.

Step Action Calculation Result

1 calculate the total package cost £10,000 + £8000 + £3000 £21,000

2 deduct the NHS voucher/PWB from the full cost N/A £21,000

3 deduct any voluntary employer contribution No voluntary contribution £21,000

4 Tech Fund applies to Desktop PC & Hearing Aid £8,000 + £3,000 £11,000

5 deduct TechFund items to determine what support threshold applies to £21,000 – £11,000 £10,000

6 deduct medium employer threshold £10,000 - £500 £9,500

7 deduct mandatory 20% cost share 20% of £9,500 £1,900

8 calculate total employer threshold & 20% mandatory cost share £500 + £1,900 £2,400

9 calculate amount for S&D eligible items £3,000 (hearing aid) + £10,000 (Wheelchair) £13,000

10 calculate amount on which S&D contribution is to be applied £13,000 - £2,400 (total applicable deductions before S&D applied) £10,600

11 calculate S&D contribution £10,600 divided by 7 x 3 £4,542.86

12 calculate AtW contribution £1,900 £14,057.14 (includes Tech Fund contribution)

Employer involvement

26. It’s the customer’s employer who will be the cost sharer, but sometimes a third party such as a provider will, contribute some or all of the cost.

27. It’s for the employer and the provider to decide who will contribute.

28. Involve employers as soon as possible in the application process and get their agreement to cost sharing before an application is approved.

Contacting the employer

29. You must first obtain the customer’s permission to disclose information, and record the outcome on the appropriate IT system, before an employer is approached.

Note: Permission can be given by different means for example, verbal, written or via an interpreter.

30. You can agree not to contact a customer’s employer, but only if there’s no requirement for the support to be used:

on the employer’s premises or

the employer isn’t required to confirm details of support received on the claim form

31. Cost sharing criteria still applies and you must be satisfied that the employer will meet the costs before you approve the application. In all cases consider appropriate review periods.

32. In all appropriate cases, an employer should be asked for a voluntary contribution whether or not cost sharing applies.

33. Any voluntary contribution made by an employer must be deducted from the total cost before you calculate any mandatory cost share contribution.

34. Always discuss with the employer the possibility of the customer taking the equipment with them if they go to another job with a new employer. Record the outcome on the AtW IT system.

Multiple employers

35. Some customers will have more than one employer at the same time, but need the same level of support for each job.

36. You must calculate the total support costs (regardless of the number of employers) and negotiate a fair cost share for all employers if the customer’s cost share status is the same for all jobs.

37. You must ensure AtW pays no more than the share expected of it as part of the total cost.

38. Ownership of equipment will depend on the type of equipment needed. For example, computer software loaded onto an employer’s system would be jointly owned as all employers would require a licence to run it.

Freelance workers

39. Customers such as actors or people with technical jobs in the arts and media industries may have a series of employers or a series of short term contracts with one employer.

40. You don’t need to approve short term contracts with each employer if you are satisfied that the customer can be classed as a freelance worker.

41. If you’re in doubt about whether the customer is a genuine freelance worker, you can ask to see supporting documents such as:

membership of a relevant professional body or union

an appointment letter from the employer

the customer’s self employed tax reference

42. Store copies of any document seen in the case file.

43. Treat freelance workers in the same way as self-employed customers and record them as self-employed on the appropriate system.

Job movers

44. You must not consider cost share in cases where the customer moves from one employer to another. This applies even if there isn’t a break between jobs, provided they apply within the first 6 weeks of starting the new job.

45. Cost share should not be considered where a customer progresses to another job within the same company such as on promotion or they are returning to work after encountering a disability whilst in employment for the first time.

46. Cost Share would be waived where the application is made either:

within the first 6 weeks in their new role (within the same company) or

within 6 weeks of returning to work following encountering a disability/health condition for the first time

47. Where someone applies to Access to Work outside of these timescales the employer would have to make the appropriate Cost Sharing contribution for that 3-year period. The customer must complete a new application and the application must be treated as a renewal and given a new AtW start date.

If the evidence was sent with a claim form, you must reply to the Payment Officer’s email, copying in their Team Leader, to confirm they are now able to make payment for the period of work.

5. If you have a task, ask your Team Leader to un-allocate the task

Note: These steps should be repeated each time the customer notifies AtW of a further period of paid work.

Actions for Payment Officers, further period of paid work claimed and evidence received with claim form

28. Customers must send evidence of any periods of paid work they wish to claim AtW support payment for. The period of work can be reported by the customer:

through the Service Centre

by email (if this is their preferred method of contact, or

by sending evidence by post or with their payment claim form

29. This can be reported by the customer through the Service Centre, email, by post (if this is their preferred method of contact) or sending evidence with their claim form.

30. If evidence of the period of work is received with a claim form, you must check if this period has been recorded in DiSC Business Case and element notes. If it hasn’t been recorded, send an email to ask for the case to be allocated to an Advisor, including the envelope ID and “Flexible application” in the subject line.

Note: the period of work must be recorded before you can make a payment.

Step Action

1 Access ATWIS and view the payment claim form and evidence

- check the customer has signed the claim form

2 If evidence is received with a payment claim form, you must access DiSC and check if the evidence has been recorded in DiSC Business Case and element notes

For example, ‘Latest period of work from xx/xx/xx to xx/xx/xx – customers must provide evidence of paid work for any claims made after this date’

If the customer has provided evidence of paid work after the dates noted, send an email to ask for the case to be allocated to an Advisor, including the envelope ID in the subject line.

Note: The Advisor will reply to your email when they have recorded the period of work in the Business Case and element notes, to confirm you can now make payment

If the payment claim form is for the period recorded in notes, go to step 3

3 Access DiSC and check Business Case and element notes to confirm if a flexible application note has been recorded.

For example, the job title ‘Freelance TV Producer (FLEXIBLE APPLICATION)’

4 Access DiSC Business Case and element notes to confirm the start and end date of the customer’s most recent period of paid work

- check if the claim has been made within the customer’s period of award

Note: AtW support can be awarded for up to 3 years using a flexible application

5 If the claim is made within the customer’s award period and the customer has provided evidence of the period of work:

- approve the claim

- make payment

- update any relevant notes with the latest paid work period

For example, ‘Latest period of work from xx/xx/xx to xx/xx/xx – customers must provide evidence of paid work for any claims made after this date’

6 If the claim is made outside of the award period or the customer has not provided evidence of the period of work:

- payment must only be made for dates that fall within the period of work

- reject payment for any dates outside of period of work

- update any relevant notes

- send email to customer

Note: if the customer doesn’t have an email address, request the documentation from DRS and return it to customer using any agreed wording

Customer has more than one employer at the same time

31. If a customer has more than one employer, both periods of work must be recorded in the DiSC Business Case and the element.

32. If the same level of support is required, the claim can continue.

33. If there is an increase in the level of support required, for example, an increase in hours of support, this must be treated as a change of circumstances and sent for allocation.

Notification of a Change in Circumstances

Action for Advisers

34. If the customer notifies AtW of a change in their circumstances or level of support:

Step Action

1 Consider the level of support required by the customer See: Assessment – Make sure the business case provides clear evidence of the customer’s flexible application and the award period is no more than the maximum 3-year length if the customer were to work every week during this period

2 If you need to consider ending a previous element – Enter a new element for the new period of support – Note: you can award support for a maximum of 3 years

3 Enter in DiSC notes: – the support in place – employer details for each period

- details of their first period of paid work and ensure additional notes for Payment Officers – For example, ‘Period of work from xx/xx/xx to xx/xx/xx – customers must provide evidence of paid work if any claims are made after this date’

4 The following must be included in the customer offer letter to support their understanding of the flexible application process: – ‘You have been given a maximum XX-year award. You do not need to make a new application each time you start a new period of paid work if your circumstances have not changed. You do need to provide us with evidence each time you have a new period of paid work. – Where your support needs change or you have a change in circumstances, you must contact AtW. – If the support agreed has a one off cost (for example, equipment) then you would be expected to take this with you if this is still appropriate for your job’

Living in Great Britain

1. Support can be applied for by anyone who:

is normally living in Great Britain (GB)

is working in GB

meets the eligibility criteria

2. Access to Work doesn’t cover:

Northern Ireland

the Channel Islands

the Isle of Man

Workers posted from the European Community

passages.quote:
Act 2010. However, where a health problem and/or a disability has resulted from their addiction and they are on a treatment programme, they are eligible to apply to Access to Work.

29. Establish if the customer is on a current treatment programme.

Note: An addiction treatment programme helps people overcome compulsive alcohol and/or drug use. The programme may take place in numerous environments, varying from residential rehab to outpatient therapy. They also range in their forms of treatment. There’s no predetermined length for addiction treatment.

30. Validation through self-declaration is sufficient evidence of being on a treatment programme. However, if doubt about eligibility or concern about fraud exists, evidence of the programme should be requested.

31. A referral for a holistic work placed assessment must be made in line with the existing AtW process.

32. AtW advisers must make applicants aware that for all areas of support (excluding mental health), their employer will be contacted ahead of the work placed assessment. This is to validate the applicant’s employment and to seek employer agreement to pay for any aids and equipment. Details of the customer’s health condition must not be divulged.

What is employment?

1. For AtW purposes, employment is:

full or part-time paid work, whether permanent, casual or temporary

a work trial arranged by DWP

work in an unsupported or supported environment

working as a councillor, elected official or appointee who has applied for a position on a public organisation’s board

work experience and self-arranged work experience

2. AtW is not available for those in:

voluntary work

training, except for training related to the customer’s paid employment and is undertaken whilst the customer is in receipt of normal wages for the job

3. To get AtW support, customers who are in work or starting work can supply one of the following:

a verbal offer of employment (check this as part of the initial employer engagement call)

a written offer of employment

a contract of employment

4. As well as one of the above, customers must be paid at least the National Minimum Wage (NMW)

See: National Minimum Wage check list on GOV.UK.

5. If during the initial contact with the customer there are doubts about the employment, ask the customer to provide supporting evidence.

6. The evidence will be considered when assessing the customer’s need for support.

7. Customers who are registered with an agency must have a job to start before they can receive support.

8. Approval cannot be given for any type of AtW support, if there’s evidence that a company is about to stop trading.

Civil servants, public servants and agency employees

9. From 1 April 2022, AtW does not fund adjustment support including assessments or equipment for civil servants with the exception of Mental Health Support Service.

Note: Public servants can continue to be considered for all support options available through AtW.

Members of the clergy

10. Applications from members of the clergy must be dealt with in exactly the same way as any other application. This is regardless of their religion.

11. The customer must be in paid employment. For example, a member of the Church of England clergy who receives a salary or stipend.

12. Some other religious denominations work on a voluntary basis. AtW is not available for voluntary workers.

13. If a customer’s employment status is in doubt, contact the employer or the religious organisations they belong to. Most contact details can be found on the internet.

What is self-employment?

1. For AtW purposes, self-employment is:

operating a business either on the customer’s own account or in partnership, or working for an employer on a self-employed contractual basis operating a franchised business on a self-employed basis

a business that satisfies the past or prospective viability tests

possessing a Unique Tax Reference number (UTR)

2. A customer is considered employed (even if they own the company) if:

they draw a salary

they pay Class 1 National Insurance contributions

3. If they pay Class 4 contributions, they are self-employed.

4. Work can be done:

from home

on their own premises

on premises owned or leased by someone else

on a travelling basis, for example a piano tuner

5. You must be satisfied that the applicant is self-employed. Do this by requesting:

a Unique Taxpayer Reference (UTR). This is a ten-digit number issued by HM Revenue & Customs

accounts for an established business

a business plan of a standard acceptable to a bank or other financial institution

6. Self-employed contractors or freelancers, such as entertainers, actors who may not see themselves as being self-employed, must provide a UTR and CV to confirm their status.

7. AtW cannot pay for the costs of setting up a business such as:

standard items of equipment

support for fact-finding

going on courses, seminars or similar events

while the business is being formed

for the purposes of turnover, Revenue Grants will be considered, Capital Grants are not considered. See HMRC link BIM40451 — Specific receipts: grants and subsidies: introduction — HMRC internal manual

Company directors

8. Customers are considered employed (not self-employed), if they pay Class 1 National Insurance contributions.

9. Company directors are not entitled to the minimum wage. They don’t therefore,have to meet this eligibility condition to get AtW support.

10. Businesses must satisfy the business viability test. This is still true even if the customer is a company director.

11. The customer must provide proof that the company is registered with Companies House.

HM Revenue and Customs checks for self-employment

12. You can rely on HM Revenue and Customs treatment of the customer’s employment circumstances. This ensures consistency when determining an applicant is self-employed.
